modules.title: “增加保存功能”怎样变成可以讨论的用户故事
用户故事需要说明什么

items.title: 先说明具体用户
items.text: 写清哪类人在什么处境中提出需求，不用“所有用户”掩盖不同人的目标和限制。

items.title: 把功能名称改成用户目标
items.text: “保存按钮”是方案，“稍后继续编辑未完成的行程”才是用户希望取得的结果。

items.title: 补充可验证的验收标准
items.text: 故事保持简短，具体范围、异常情况和完成条件再写入 {c:acceptance-criteria} 或对应 {c:use-case}。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: {c:user-story} 是需求讨论的起点，不是完整规格。它说明用户、目标和原因；{c:use-case} 继续描述用户与系统怎样交互，{c:acceptance-criteria} 说明成果必须满足哪些条件。

lessonPractice.title: 团队准备增加“保存行程”功能。下面哪一条最适合作为用户故事？

options.label: 作为正在规划多日旅行的人，我希望保存未完成的行程，以便稍后继续编辑
options.feedback: 对。这句话说明了谁有需要、希望完成什么，以及这个能力带来的结果，可以继续讨论保存范围和验收条件。

options.label: 新增 saveTrip() 方法、数据库表和右上角蓝色按钮
options.feedback: 这是实现与界面清单。团队仍然不知道谁需要保存、为什么需要，也无法据此判断哪些方案合适。

options.label: 增加一个体验更好的行程保存功能
options.feedback: 这只是功能名称和模糊评价，没有说明目标用户、使用目的，也没有给后续讨论提供明确边界。

en.title: A team plans to add trip saving. Which option works best as a user story?

options.label: As a traveler planning a multi-day trip, I want to save an unfinished itinerary so I can continue editing it later
options.feedback: Correct. It names the user, goal, and value, giving the team a useful starting point for discussing scope and acceptance criteria.

options.label: Add a saveTrip() method, a database table, and a blue button in the top right
options.feedback: That is an implementation and interface list. It does not explain who needs the feature or why.

options.label: Add a better trip-saving experience
options.feedback: That is only a feature label with a vague quality claim. It does not identify the user, goal, or value.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请把“保存行程”整理成用户故事，分别写清目标用户、想完成的事和原因。只使用我已经提供的事实；缺少用户依据或业务规则时列成待确认问题。整理后再补充可以直接检查的验收标准，不要提前决定按钮位置和数据库结构。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Turn “save a trip” into a user story that states the target user, goal, and reason. Use only the facts I provide, and list unsupported user claims or business rules as open questions. Then add directly checkable acceptance criteria without deciding the button position or database structure.

learning.assumes: You have seen feature requests such as “add a save button” without a clear user or problem.
learning.outcome: You can turn a feature idea into a user story with a user, goal, and reason, then identify the acceptance criteria and business rules still missing.

modules.title: Turn “add saving” into a user story the team can discuss
What a user story needs to state

items.title: Name a specific user
items.text: Describe the person and situation instead of hiding different needs behind “all users.”

items.title: Replace the feature label with a goal
items.text: A save button is a solution; continuing an unfinished itinerary later is the result the user needs.

items.title: Add checkable conditions separately
items.text: Keep the story brief, then put scope, exceptions, and completion conditions in {c:acceptance-criteria} or a {c:use-case}.

modules.title: What people often confuse
modules.text: A {c:user-story} starts the conversation. A {c:use-case} describes the interaction, while {c:acceptance-criteria} state what the result must satisfy.
